title: Where to put a new city hall
script: Narrator: When the city hall in a mid-sized city became too old to repair, the council first proposed building a new one on farmland at the edge of town, where land was cheap. Residents objected that the site could only be reached easily by car, which would make it hard for elderly people and students to attend public meetings. The council then suggested renting space in a shopping mall downtown instead. That idea was also rejected, after lawyers pointed out that the city could not guarantee access to the building outside the mall's business hours. In the end, the council voted to rebuild on the original site in the city center, while moving staff into temporary offices in a former school for three years. The mayor admits that this option will take the longest, but she argues that a city hall should stand where every resident can reach it without difficulty.
translation: ある中規模の都市で市役所が古くなり修理できなくなったとき、市議会は当初、土地が安い町はずれの農地に新しい庁舎を建てることを提案した。住民は、その場所には車でなければ行きにくく、高齢者や学生が公開の会議に出席しにくくなると反対した。そこで議会は、代わりに中心街のショッピングモールの一角を借りることを提案した。しかしこの案も、モールの営業時間外には市が建物に入れることを保証できないと弁護士が指摘したため、却下された。最終的に議会は、職員を3年間かつての学校の仮庁舎に移したうえで、市の中心部にある元の場所に建て直すことを議決した。市長は、この案がもっとも時間がかかることを認めつつも、市役所はすべての住民が苦労せずに行ける場所に建つべきだと主張している。

questions.question: What did the council finally decide to do?
choices: Construct a new building where the old one stood.
Build a new city hall on farmland outside town.
Rent offices inside a downtown shopping mall.
Move its departments permanently into a former school.
questions.explanation: 「In the end, the council voted to rebuild on the original site in the city center」とあり、最終的には元の場所に建て直すことになった。町はずれの農地に建てる案と、ショッピングモールを借りる案は、どちらも却下された案。かつての学校は「temporary offices ... for three years」とあるように一時的な移転先で、恒久的に移るわけではない。

questions.question: Why was the shopping mall plan rejected?
choices: Residents could only reach the mall easily by car.
The building might not be open whenever the city needed it.
The rent was higher than the cost of new construction.
Shop owners refused to share their space with city staff.
questions.explanation: 「the city could not guarantee access to the building outside the mall's business hours」とあり、営業時間外に建物を使えないおそれがあったため却下された。車でなければ行きにくいというのは、農地の案に対する住民の反対理由。家賃が建設費より高い、店主が場所の共有を拒んだ、は本文にない。

title: Volunteers counting winter birds
script: Narrator: Every winter, thousands of volunteers in North America spend a day counting the birds they see and sending their results to researchers. The project began more than a century ago as an alternative to a holiday hunting tradition, and today it produces one of the longest records of bird populations in the world. Scientists have used the data to show that many species are shifting their winter ranges northward. At first, some researchers doubted that amateurs could identify birds accurately. However, studies comparing volunteer counts with those of experts found that the overall trends matched closely, although beginners did tend to miss rare species. To reduce such errors, organizers now pair new volunteers with experienced ones and ask everyone to upload photos of unusual sightings. Because the project depends entirely on people giving up their free time, organizers are worried that few younger people have joined in recent years and that the average age of participants keeps rising.
translation: 毎年冬になると、北米の何千人ものボランティアが1日かけて目にした鳥を数え、その結果を研究者に送る。この活動は1世紀以上前に、祝日の狩猟の習慣に代わるものとして始まり、今では世界でもっとも長期にわたる鳥の個体数の記録の一つとなっている。科学者はこのデータを使って、多くの種が越冬する範囲を北へ移していることを示してきた。当初、一部の研究者は、素人が鳥を正確に見分けられるのか疑っていた。しかし、ボランティアの集計と専門家の集計を比べた研究では、全体の傾向はよく一致していた。ただし、初心者は珍しい種を見落としがちだった。こうした誤りを減らすため、主催者は現在、新しいボランティアを経験者と組ませ、全員に珍しい鳥を見かけたら写真をアップロードするよう求めている。この活動は人々が自由な時間を割いてくれることに全面的に頼っているため、主催者は、近年若い人がほとんど参加せず、参加者の平均年齢が上がり続けていることを心配している。

questions.question: What does the speaker say about the accuracy of the volunteers' counts?
choices: They are too unreliable to be used in serious scientific studies.
They reflect general patterns well but can overlook uncommon birds.
They are more precise than the counts made by professional experts.
They became accurate only after hunters joined the project.
questions.explanation: 「the overall trends matched closely, although beginners did tend to miss rare species」をまとめると、全体の傾向は正しく表すが珍しい鳥を見落とすことがある、となる。科学に使えないほど不正確というのは、当初の「some researchers doubted」で、後の研究で否定された内容。専門家より正確、狩猟をする人が加わってから正確になった、は本文にない。

questions.question: What concern do the organizers have about the project's future?
choices: Photos of unusual birds are becoming difficult to verify.
Birds may soon move too far north to be counted at all.
It may struggle to attract enough participants in coming years.
Experienced volunteers are unwilling to train new members.
questions.explanation: 「the project depends entirely on people giving up their free time」と「few younger people have joined in recent years and ... the average age of participants keeps rising」をつなぐと、将来、十分な参加者を集められなくなるおそれがあると分かる。写真の確認が難しい、鳥が北へ移りすぎて数えられない、経験者が新人の指導を嫌がる、は本文にない。

title: Saving a mountain town's harvest festival
script: Narrator: For over two hundred years, a mountain town has held a harvest festival on the last weekend of September. Recently, however, the organizing committee has struggled to find enough young people to carry the heavy wooden shrines through the streets. The committee first announced that the festival would be cut from two days to one. Local shop owners protested, saying the second day brought in most of their visitors, so that plan was withdrawn. Next, the committee proposed hiring professional carriers from outside the town, but elders insisted that only people with ties to the town should carry the shrines. Finally, an agreement was reached: the festival will keep both days, but the shrines will be moved on lighter wheeled carts, and students from a nearby university who join the town's preservation society will be allowed to help. Some elders still feel uneasy about the carts, but most residents say the change is better than losing the festival altogether.
translation: ある山あいの町では、200年以上にわたり、9月の最終週末に収穫祭が開かれてきた。しかし最近、実行委員会は、重い木製の神輿を担いで通りを練り歩く若者を十分に集められずにいる。委員会は当初、祭りを2日間から1日に短縮すると発表した。地元の商店主は、2日目に訪れる客がもっとも多いと言って抗議し、この案は撤回された。次に委員会は、町の外から専門の担ぎ手を雇うことを提案したが、長老たちは町と縁のある人だけが神輿を担ぐべきだと主張した。最終的に合意がまとまった。祭りは2日間のまま行うが、神輿は車輪の付いた軽い台車で運び、町の保存会に入った近くの大学の学生も手伝えるようにするというものだ。長老の中には台車にまだ不安を感じる人もいるが、ほとんどの住民は、祭りそのものを失うよりはこの変更のほうがよいと言っている。

questions.question: What has the committee finally decided about the procession?
choices: The shrines will travel on carts, with student helpers allowed.
The procession will be held on just one of the two days.
Paid carriers from other areas will carry the heavy shrines.
Only elders will be allowed to take part in the procession.
questions.explanation: 「the shrines will be moved on lighter wheeled carts, and students from a nearby university who join the town's preservation society will be allowed to help」が最終的な合意。1日に短縮する案は商店主の抗議で撤回され、外部の専門の担ぎ手を雇う案は長老の反対で採用されなかった。長老だけが参加できる、は本文にない。

questions.question: Why was the plan to shorten the festival withdrawn?
choices: Elders insisted that only local people should carry the shrines.
Young residents offered to carry the shrines after all.
The festival was moved to a different weekend in autumn.
Businesses relied on the visitors who came on the second day.
questions.explanation: 「Local shop owners protested, saying the second day brought in most of their visitors, so that plan was withdrawn」とあり、商店が2日目の客に頼っていたため撤回された。地元の人だけが担ぐべきだというのは、外部の担ぎ手を雇う案に対する長老の反対理由。若者が結局担ぐと申し出た、別の週末に移した、は本文にない。

title: Social prescribing
script: Narrator: In some countries, doctors have begun offering what is called social prescribing. Instead of only giving medicine, a doctor may refer a patient to a gardening club, an art class, or a walking group. The idea comes from the observation that many people who visit clinics repeatedly are not seriously ill but are lonely or under stress. Early programs reported that patients who joined such activities visited their doctors less often. Critics, however, noted that most of these programs were small and that the people who chose to take part may already have been more motivated than others. More recent studies with larger groups have found smaller benefits, though still positive ones. Supporters also point out that the programs work only when local communities have enough clubs and volunteers, which is often not the case in poorer areas. For this reason, some health officials argue that funding for community groups should be treated as part of the health budget.
translation: 一部の国では、医師が「社会的処方」と呼ばれるものを始めている。薬を出すだけでなく、医師は患者をガーデニングのクラブや美術教室、ウォーキングの会に紹介することがある。この考えは、何度も診療所を訪れる人の多くが、重い病気ではなく、孤独だったりストレスを抱えていたりするという観察から生まれた。初期の取り組みでは、こうした活動に参加した患者は医師にかかる回数が減ったと報告された。しかし批判する人は、そうした取り組みの多くが小規模で、自ら参加を選んだ人はもともと他の人より意欲が高かった可能性があると指摘した。より多くの人を対象にした最近の研究では、効果はより小さいものの、やはり良い効果が見られた。支持者はまた、この取り組みは地域に十分なクラブやボランティアがある場合にしか機能せず、貧しい地域ではそうでないことが多いと指摘する。このため、一部の保健当局者は、地域の団体への資金を保健予算の一部として扱うべきだと主張している。

questions.question: What does the speaker say about the evidence for social prescribing?
choices: Its advantages appear more modest than early reports suggested.
It has been shown to replace medicine for most patients.
Larger studies found that it brought no benefits at all.
It works best for patients who have serious illnesses.
questions.explanation: 初期の報告(「patients who joined such activities visited their doctors less often」)に対し、「More recent studies with larger groups have found smaller benefits, though still positive ones」とあり、効果は当初の報告より控えめだと分かる。大規模な研究で効果がまったくなかった、は「still positive ones」で否定されている。多くの患者で薬の代わりになる、重い病気の患者に最も効く、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why do some health officials want community groups funded from the health budget?
choices: Doctors are refusing to prescribe medicine to lonely patients.
Programs fail where there are too few local activities to join.
Community groups currently charge patients very high fees.
Gardening clubs have proven more effective than any drug.
questions.explanation: 「the programs work only when local communities have enough clubs and volunteers, which is often not the case in poorer areas」を受けて「For this reason」と続くので、参加できる地域の活動が足りない所では取り組みが機能しないことが理由。医師が薬の処方を拒んでいる、団体が高い料金を取っている、ガーデニングがどの薬よりも効く、は本文にない。

title: Rules for rental e-scooters
script: Narrator: When rental electric scooters arrived in a European city, they quickly became popular with young commuters, but pedestrians complained about scooters left blocking sidewalks. The city council first planned to ban the scooters completely. Before the vote, however, a transport study showed that many riders had stopped driving for short trips, so the ban was put aside. The council then announced a limit on the number of scooters each company could operate. This plan was later dropped as well, because companies said they would simply place all their remaining scooters in the busiest areas. Under the rules now in force, scooters may be parked only in marked zones, and riders who leave them elsewhere continue to pay rental fees until they come back and park them properly. Officials report that complaints have fallen sharply, although they say they will review the rules again next year, once data on injuries becomes available.
translation: ヨーロッパのある都市にレンタルの電動キックボードが登場すると、若い通勤者の間ですぐに人気になったが、歩行者は歩道をふさぐように放置されたキックボードに苦情を言った。市議会は当初、キックボードを全面的に禁止する予定だった。しかし採決の前に、交通調査によって多くの利用者が短い移動で車を運転しなくなったことが示され、禁止は見送られた。次に議会は、各社が運用できる台数に上限を設けると発表した。しかしこの案も後に取りやめになった。各社が、残りの台数をすべて最も混雑する地域に置くだけだと言ったからだ。現在施行されている規則では、キックボードは指定された区域にしか止めることができず、それ以外の場所に置いた利用者は、戻ってきて正しく止めるまで利用料金を払い続ける。当局によると苦情は大きく減ったが、けがに関するデータがそろう来年に、規則をもう一度見直すという。

questions.question: What rule is currently in effect for the scooters?
choices: They are banned from all of the city's streets entirely.
Each company may run only a limited number of them.
They must be left only in specially marked parking areas.
They may be used only by commuters during rush hour.
questions.explanation: 「Under the rules now in force, scooters may be parked only in marked zones」とあり、現在は指定区域にだけ止められる。全面禁止は採決前に見送られた案で、各社の台数の上限は後に取りやめになった案。通勤時間帯に通勤者だけが使える、は本文にない。

questions.question: Why did the council decide against a complete ban?
choices: Companies threatened to move scooters to the busiest areas.
Pedestrians said the scooters were no longer a problem.
Injury data showed that scooters were safer than cars.
Evidence showed that riders were making fewer short car trips.
questions.explanation: 「a transport study showed that many riders had stopped driving for short trips, so the ban was put aside」とあり、利用者が短い移動で車を使わなくなったという調査結果が理由。各社が混雑地域に移すと言ったのは、台数の上限の案が取りやめになった理由。歩行者がもう問題ないと言った、は本文にない。けがのデータは来年そろう予定で、まだ出ていない。
